251577d1005fddcc25de4aaf30205970eae4cb1b.caption: The concept of Maximum Text Width in a UI design system. It shows a block of text with a maximum width of 34em, which is based on the font size used. The text block demonstrates that to maintain optimal readability, the text should not exceed 80 characters per line.

4053964a226eb05f2d533ac30e70b0b9032700b6.caption: Maximum text widths for different font sizes in the STIHL Design System. Callout 1 points to a heading in Uppercase with a font size of 26px, showing a maximum length of 884px. Callout 2 points to a text in Text M with a font size of 16px, showing a maximum length of 544px. Callout 3 points to a text in Utility XS Demi with a font size of 12px, showing a maximum length of 408px. Each measurement refers to the maximum length calculated as font size multiplied by 34em.

59889748f4582e61accaa77691f60d1b6b33e828.caption: The concept of maximum text width within content areas using two viewport examples: one at 1024px and another at 1440px. Callout 1 points to a viewport of 1024px where the container width is smaller than the maximum text width, so the container width is used. Callout 2 points to a viewport of 1440px where the container width is larger than the maximum text width, so the text is capped at its maximum allowed width to ensure optimal readability.

e52181595dcad1d21c656a657973a927fb350799.caption: The layout for Content-Heavy Pages (Reading-Focused) in the STIHL Design System. It shows a headline and body text both constrained to a maximum width of 544 pixels, which is derived from a font size of 16 pixels multiplied by 34 em units. This alignment ensures visual consistency and a harmonious reading experience by preventing oversized headlines from disrupting the text rhythm. The body text is labeled as Text M with a font size of 16px, and the heading is labeled as Heading L, both adhering to the same maximum width.
